overview: The screens, menus and keys the other mods here use to talk to you.
Press N for questions waiting on you, J for action menus, /pandorical mods for the rest.

15.26.2: A player not trusted with fire can still light a nether portal: flint and steel or a fire charge on an empty frame makes the portal, never fire.
15.26.1: A structure's waterlogged blocks keep their water while it moves, so a ship's waterlogged slabs and stairs no longer sail off dry.
15.26.0: A mod's creature with its own body can flinch when it is hit, with a hurt animation of its own.
15.25.0: Joining a server you have joined before skips downloading its textures, models and sounds: your game keeps the last few servers' sets and the server only sends them when they have changed.
Servers no longer hand out Pandorical or other client mods, and the game no longer offers to install them. Keep your mods up to date with your launcher.
A slow download of a server's textures no longer trips a timer meant for older servers partway through joining.
15.24.4: A server running Pandorical from CurseForge keeps no client mods for players either. Elsewhere nothing changes.
15.24.3: Pandorical from CurseForge takes no client mods from servers: update it and your other client mods from CurseForge. Elsewhere nothing changes.
15.24.2: The newer-mods notice has an Install and quit button that does just that, with no second question.
15.24.1: Blocks drawn by what stands beside them, joined glass, rail diagonals, door jambs and the rest, now show with Sodium installed too, where before they fell back to their plain look.
An arena that makes its own PvP rules, like PvP Dimensions' arenas, makes its own fire and explosives rules too: what an op has not trusted a player with is theirs to use in there.
15.24.0: Immersive portals, a server setting an op or a mod can turn on: a nether portal shows what is past it through the swirl, and you step through in half a second instead of standing in it for four.
The trip itself is one swirl: it thickens as you go in, covers the change of world where the loading screen was, and thins on the far side, with a squelch each way. Your own settings can turn it off.
15.23.0: Glass from a server mod such as Better Glass can join up with the same glass beside it, drawn as one clear sheet instead of a grid of framed blocks.
15.22.3: A game whose folder is a link to somewhere else, as a launcher's instance can be, takes the mods a server keeps for it again. It used to turn every update down without saying so.
15.22.2: A mod's key that shares the game's Quick Actions key works again: G poops again with Poopsmith, instead of opening the menus. The menus are still on their own key.
15.22.0: A server mod can ask your game for a picture of the world from somewhere other than where you stand, such as a camera set down in the world. Your game draws it out of sight, so you see nothing of it, even with a menu open.

Playing without Pandorical, on Bedrock through Geyser too, the mods list, settings, notices, the welcome, what's new and trust open as the game's own forms. /pandorical actions, or the game's Quick Actions, has them all in one place.
The mods list no longer shows the libraries packed inside other mods.
15.21.0: A mod can add a mob the game has nothing like: drawn from its own model, with its own animations - idle, swimming or walking, striking - and its own size, rather than dressed up as a vanilla mob.
Such a mob can carry values of its own, which used to garble every client it was sent to.
Players without Pandorical are shown a stand-in vanilla mob for it only if that mob can read it; otherwise they are not sent it at all.
Installing the mods a server sends you closes the game, since the running game keeps the old ones until it restarts.
A server tells you in chat when your game is running an older mod than the one it sent you.
15.20.3: A mod's new mob is drawn in its own skin and shape every time; joining sometimes lost them and drew the plain vanilla mob.
Its young are drawn small, not their parents' size.
In singleplayer, a mod's new mob keeps its own size and strength rather than the vanilla mob's it is built on.
15.20.2: The question to install the client mods a server keeps for you appears again; on 26.3 it failed every time, so nothing was ever installed.
It also appears in the pause menu and on the screen you are sent back to, for a game that joins a server as it starts and never shows the title screen.
Switching one of your mods on or off from the Mods screen works again too.
15.20.1: The server log says which Pandorical, Fabric API and mods each player's game is running when they join.
Ops can ask the same in game with /pandorical clients.
15.20.0: Server mods can add new mobs, and you see them in their own skins with nothing else to install.
Players without Pandorical are shown a vanilla mob in their place, or nothing, as the mod chooses.
15.19.1: The server keeps your Fabric API at its own version too, the same way it keeps Pandorical.
15.19.0: A server can keep client mods for you: a newer Pandorical, and any client-only mods it carries. Joining downloads them, and back at the title screen or server list the game asks before installing. Switch one off from Mods and it stays off.
15.18.1: Standing still on a ship at sea, you and everyone else aboard stand still, instead of walking on the spot at the ship's speed.
15.18.0: A mod can keep the sea out of part of a structure: Big Boats keeps a ship's hold dry while she sails, so you walk it in air instead of swimming.
15.17.0: A mod can put a button on the first page J opens, beside the menus rather than inside Server. Learning Blocks does.
An action menu button can wear a picture of a mod's own instead of an item. Particle Emote's buttons show the particles they throw.
Perspective on the Game menu offers the three views to pick from, instead of stepping to the next one.

The Server menu starts with Welcome, What's new and Mods. /pandorical changes shows what changed since you were last here, or what each mod changed last. Server wears a beacon on the menu of menus, and Game a grass block.
A menu button for somebody asks who by face, from everyone else online, instead of needing a name typed.
15.16.0: A server mod can draw a mob in its own shape: new parts, or the mob's own resized, still walking and fighting as it always did. Baby Skeletons uses it for skeletons shaped like babies.
15.15.0: A server mod's camera, like Redstone Photography's, takes its picture from your own screen, without the HUD or your hand, as F1 then F2 would.
15.14.0: Wide fence gates are drawn piece by piece as their blocks swing out, for More Doors.
Joined fence gates are drawn from one model per shape, turned to face the way the gate does.
15.13.0: A ladder or vine on a ship at sea climbs the same as one on land.
Blocks on a ship at sea can be clicked, for a mod that says which: Big Boats opens its doors, chests, furnaces and crafting tables this way.
15.12.0: Ops can trust players one by one with PvP, fire and lava, explosives, and hurting others' animals, on a page /pandorical trust opens.
Each switch has a default for everyone; PvP's is the server's own pvp gamerule.
15.11.0: A setting whose options are shapes can show the shape beside its name in the mods menu.
15.10.0: The mods screen puts the mods only you are running at the top, above the server's hundred.
A client-only mod like Sodium was listed all along, as row one hundred and nine.
15.9.0: Opening the notice tray puts the badge out, even if you answered nothing. Looking is enough.
It comes back when something new arrives.
On a controller the badge names your button instead of telling you to press a key.
15.8.0: The welcome is offered until you have actually read it, not just until it has been shown once.
Anyone who was busy when it first arrived gets it again on their next login.
15.7.0: The notice badge shows what is waiting, not just a bell.
15.6.0: The notice badge shrinks once you have opened the tray. The key is on it the first time only.
15.5.0: In the notice tray, summaries wrap, answers line up down one edge, and the time left shows.
15.4.0: Buttons that close a screen work again.
What changed since you were away wraps instead of running off the panel.
The notice badge names the key you actually have bound.
15.3.1: What changed since you were away is readable. It was grey on grey.
The notice badge sits above the hotbar instead of under it.
15.3.0: The notice badge moved to the bottom right, out of the crowded corner.
The notice tray reads as a list of questions, and has a way out.
15.2.0: The notice tray opens on N, or the d-pad's right on a controller.
The badge in the corner is readable and names its key.
15.1.1: Fixed the notice badge drawing as a sliver in the corner.
15.1.0: Notices: a mod can put a question to you in a tray of its own instead of in chat.
The death screen's buttons work on a client that has stopped ticking.
Horses turn the way you press, at a horse's pace.
Grass slabs no longer flash white as they are placed.
15.0.0: Action menus: grids of buttons on one key. Press J, or set your own.
The mods screen lists what you are running and can switch your own mods off.
Notices: questions from mods wait in a tray on N instead of scrolling past in chat.
